confidence_score_justification.overall_75_floor: 75 = weighted avg of 5 sub-scores (pulse, offset, feed, epack, geometry). At 75+, the worst sub-score is no lower than 60, meaning no single physics dimension is speculative. Based on: ≥3 published sources corroborate each parameter, and ≥1 real-world program validates it.
confidence_score_justification.multi_material_65_floor: 65 allows one sub-score at 50 (no published data for that dimension on this material). SS/Al have fewer published EDM cutting condition tables than D2. The 10-point relaxation acknowledges data sparsity, not lower physics confidence.
confidence_score_justification.operator_trust_threshold: Below 60, at least 2 sub-scores are speculative — too risky for a chargeable product. Above 80, all sub-scores are corroborated — aspirational for V2.

charging_scope_v1.title: PRISM Wire EDM — Mitsubishi Straight Die Cut Program Generator (V1)

charging_scope_v1.caveat: Operator review required before first run — program is a validated starting point, not a guaranteed first-part-right

philosophy: Scope narrowly, prove deeply, launch honestly. It is better to charge for a narrow scope that is demonstrably correct than to claim broad capability that fails when a machinist runs it. V1 is Mitsubishi straight die cuts only. V2 adds taper. V3 adds other controllers.

U-WLAUNCH01.title: Multi-thickness D2 validation: 25.4mm / 50mm / 100mm — tests + proof
U-WLAUNCH01.description: Write and run cwedm-validation-d2-multithick.test.ts. For D2 at 25.4mm, 50mm, 100mm: (1) generate a complete program, (2) assert feed rate within 10-15% of published Lemhunter values, (3) assert H-offsets decrease monotonically, (4) assert E-pack = E12X1-E12X4 (group 1, thickness code matches), (5) assert Ra_predicted within 20% of Klocke, (6) assert confidence_score.feed >= 70, (7) verify that 100mm program has more passes than 50mm program (physics must drive this). This DIRECTLY proves the calibration fixes from the current session are correct.

four_loop.build: Write test file using WEDMPrintToProgramEngine with pre-parsed contours (skip DXF for speed). Run 3 thickness cases.
four_loop.scrutinize: /prism-review — verify test assertions are physics-grounded, not just plausibility checks
four_loop.gap_fill: If any case fails, diagnose: is it the piecewise feed model, E-pack code, or offset chain? Fix at root cause.
four_loop.tie_up: Test output includes actual vs expected table for all 3 thicknesses. Reference cited for each expected value.

abort_criteria: Feed rate at 25mm < 1.0 mm/min (unreasonably slow) or > 8.0 mm/min (too fast for D2)
E-pack codes not in E1221-E1244 range for D2
H-offsets are NOT monotonically decreasing across passes
Confidence score below 60 for all 3 cases (suggests systematic physics error)

rollback.procedure: rm src/__tests__/cwedm-validation-d2-multithick.test.ts — test file only, no engine changes

U-WLAUNCH01.exit_criteria: 3/3 D2 thickness cases pass all 7 assertions. Feed rates cited against published Lemhunter values.

U-WLAUNCH02.title: Multi-material validation: 304SS / 6061 / WC / Inconel at 25.4mm
U-WLAUNCH02.description: Write and run cwedm-validation-multimaterial.test.ts. For 304SS, 6061-T6, WC carbide, Inconel 718 at 25.4mm: (1) assert correct material group in E-pack (2=SS, 3=Al, 5=carbide, 7=superalloy), (2) assert feed rates follow material hierarchy: Al > C_steel > SS > Inconel (physics-correct ordering), (3) assert WC gets ≥ 5 passes for Ra 0.8µm (carbide needs more passes due to brittleness), (4) assert Inconel feed < D2 feed × 0.6 (mrr_factor 0.5 vs D2 0.9 — Inconel has extreme erosion resistance), (5) assert confidence >= 65 for all (SS, Al have less published data). This proves generality beyond D2.

four_loop.scrutinize: /prism-review — verify material hierarchy is physics-correct, not arbitrary
four_loop.gap_fill: If carbide pass count is wrong, check EDMMultiPassStrategyEngine material hardness factor for WC. If Inconel feed is wrong, check mrr_factor in material definition.
four_loop.tie_up: Test includes source citation for each material's expected behavior.

U-WLAUNCH04.title: Extend E-pack condition code to range 1-9 (CHOCTAW pattern)
U-WLAUNCH04.description: The CHOCTAW DEFENSE cannelure program uses E1281 — condition code 8. Our current model caps at 5. Mitsubishi FA/MV machines support conditions 1-9. Extend resolveEPackConditionCode() to cover the full range: 6=precision fine, 7=mirror, 8=ultra precision, 9=optical quality. These are very narrow Ra bands (<0.1µm). Update tests in wedm-epack-generator.test.ts. This also explains the CHOCTAW program's unusual feed (F.06) — they were using an ultra-precision condition on a thread form.

four_loop.gap_fill: Update wedm-epack-generator.test.ts tests for new conditions. Run full suite — must stay at 216+ pass.
four_loop.tie_up: Add note: conditions 6-9 are optical quality — rarely used in production die work.

U-WLAUNCH04.exit_criteria: Conditions 1-9 supported. CHOCTAW E1281 now generatable. E1221 for Ra 0.8µm still correct. All tests pass.

U-WLAUNCH05.title: Taper skim cascade split: increasing vs decreasing speed pattern
U-WLAUNCH05.description: NOZE TEST (taper program) shows increasing skim speeds: F.16 → .23 → .26 → .30 in/min. ITW SHAKEPROOF (straight program) shows decreasing: F.12 → .24 → .21 → .20. Our current calibration (max(2.0 - 0.15*(p-2), 1.2)) uses the ITW decreasing pattern for ALL programs. PHYSICS CAVEAT: the increasing taper cascade is EMPIRICALLY OBSERVED from real programs, not yet derived from first principles. Hypothesized mechanism: taper reduces effective spark contact area per pass, requiring higher feed to maintain MRR. This is a V1 empirical fit, not a proven model — document this limitation. Implement: if taper_angle_deg > 0, use increasing cascade. If 0, use decreasing. Add a test validating both patterns.

four_loop.build: Add taper_angle_deg check to EDMMultiPassStrategyEngine.ts skim speed computation (2 locations). When taper > 0: speedFactor = 1.5 + 0.15*(p-2). When 0: existing max(2.0 - 0.15*(p-2), 1.2).
four_loop.scrutinize: /prism-review — verify taper speedFactor produces NOZE-like pattern (increasing). Verify straight produces ITW-like pattern (decreasing).
four_loop.gap_fill: Add tests: taper case → skim2 > skim1 speed. Straight case → skim speeds decrease after skim1.
four_loop.tie_up: Both patterns documented with source citations (ITW SHAKEPROOF and NOZE TEST real programs).

abort_criteria: Taper cascade change breaks non-taper test cases
Cannot find taper_angle_deg flowing through to skim speed calculation
Physics rationale for increasing taper cascade cannot be documented
U-WLAUNCH05.exit_criteria: Taper programs: skim speeds increase pass-over-pass. Straight programs: skim speeds decrease. Both patterns tested. NOZE TEST pattern reproduced.

U-WLAUNCH07.title: Scope guard: V1 scope enforcement + clear limitation messages
U-WLAUNCH07.description: Add scope enforcement to WEDMPrintToProgramEngine.ts. If (1) taper_angle_deg > 5°: return error 'V1 does not support taper programs — use U/V axis programs require V2 (planned Q2 2026)'. If (2) controller is not mitsubishi: return warning 'Condition codes for Sodick/Makino/Fanuc/AgieCharmilles are in development — output will be structurally correct but technology codes require operator verification'. If (3) geometry has > 1 re-entrant pocket (estimated from segment angles): return warning 'Thread form / re-entrant geometry detected — feed rates may be 40-60% lower than predicted; reduce to F.06 in/min if wire breaks occur'. These messages protect operator trust by being honest.

four_loop.build: Add scope checks at top of WEDMPrintToProgramEngine.ts generate() method. Return structured errors/warnings, not silently compute wrong output.
four_loop.scrutinize: /prism-review — verify error messages are actionable, cite V2 timeline
four_loop.gap_fill: Test: taper input → correct error. Non-Mitsubishi → correct warning. Complex geometry → warning.
four_loop.tie_up: Warnings added to result.warnings[] array AND to setup sheet.

U-WLAUNCH07.exit_criteria: Taper rejected with helpful message. Non-Mitsubishi warns. Re-entrant geometry warned. All V1 valid inputs still work.
